text: Hi Jules, thanks for writing. Never mind my friend, don't worry me. Politely I answer in all seriousness, or otherwise not. Public debt is owed by the feds to multiple parties, mostly to other countries. China and Japan have a combined amount of $1.1T, quite substantial, but do not hold a majority. Canada, UK, Belgium, etc., are there too. But the most debt of all is the US fed fund debt owed to American people. 30% is held by private individuals (and family trusts) in the US, and other 30% held in retirement funds (like mutual funds, pension schemes, Fidelity, Vanguard etc.) and mutual life insurance etc. So, the debt is massive and a huge part of it is within the US, so self-funded. Which has its implications but not bearable just yet. Let's talk sometime. Take care, Andy
